newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IEB shares drop after 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: IEB shares drop after 1996 results.

text.p: The shares in Hungary's Inter-Europa Bank (IEB) opened lower on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Thursday following the release of its preliminary unconsolidated 1996 results this morning.

IEB shares opened at 48,950 forints, below Wednesday's close of 50,500 forints, as many of the market's leading issues moved lower continuing yesterday's trend. At 1201 GMT IEB shares traded at 49,000 forints, down 1,500.
IEB, member of Italy's Gruppo Bancario San Paolo reported a pre-tax profit of 2.086 billion forints for 1996 against a pre-tax profit of 1.78 billion forints for 1995.
The bank's net interest income shrank to 3.25 billion forints from 3.77 billion, the bank's earnings report said.
"In 1996 we operated in fierce competition," IEB's General Director, Pier Franco Rubatto, told a news conference. "The trends benefited our clients as interest rates were declining," he said.
In 1996 Hungarian interest rates fell some ten percent from around 30 percent at the beginning of the year.
"It's more difficult to protect certain market conditions when interest rates are falling than when they're rising," Rubatto said.

Last year the bank's balance sheet total grew to 90.85 billion forints from 62.39 billion at the end of 1995. Clients' deposits rose 54 percent to 39 billion forints, of which retail clients accounted for 12 billion forints.
"This means the bank has significantly reduced its dependence on the interbank money market," the report said.
IEB, billed by Rubatto a "small to medium (size) bank" had over 12,000 clients last years, of which 4,500 were retail clients.
Speaking about the bank's plans for 1997, Rubatto said profitability will receive special attention.
"We have to pay particularly strong attention to profitability, more (attention) than on the growth of balance sheet total," he said.

"Our minimum requirement is to exceed the growth rate of inflation what we forecast to remain below 20 percent in 1997," Rubatto said, adding that the pre-tax profit plan was 2.5 billion forints for 1997.
The government's inflation target for 1997 is around 17 percent.
Inter-Europa Bank will hold its annual shareholders meeting on April 24, with the raise of the current 2.81 billion forint issued share capital on the agenda.
"In the first step we'd raise our capital via a bonus share issue, while the second step would be a public share issue," Rubatto said.

The bonus share issue is to be financed from profit reserves, while the public share issue aims at bringing IEB's 1996-end 9.37 billion forints shareholders' capital (issued share capital and reserves) to above 10 billion.

In 1997 the bank wishes to pay more attention to gain Spanish companies operating in Hungary as its clients following that Spain's Banco Santander acquired what the earnings report called "substantial stake" in it.
"As a result the bank set up a 'Spanish Desk' to handle Spanish clients."
-- Emese Bartha, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327-4040
